endpoints.summary: Patient self-books an appointment. Resolves the PhysicianProfile from the body's physicianUserId, rejects an exact same-day same-startTime collision for that physician, creates the Appointment as PENDING with patientUserId = the CALLER, then fires a best-effort notification + email to the physician. Returns the created row with clinic.name, physician.user.displayName and subprofile.
endpoints.auth: router.use(authCheck) at L19 — JWT Bearer only (jwt.verify of process.env.JWT_SECRET, no DB lookup). NO aiUsageCheck, NO auditLog anywhere in this router. NO in-handler userType or ownership gate: any authenticated user (patient, physician, staff, manager) may call this and it books THEM as the patient. clinicId ownership and clinic.allowPatientBooking are never checked here.
endpoints.responseShape:
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "clinicId": "uuid",
  "physicianId": "uuid",          // PhysicianProfile.id, NOT the physicianUserId that was sent
  "patientUserId": "uuid",          // always req.user.id
  "subprofileId": "uuid" | null,
  "clinicPatientId": null,          // never set by this handler
  "status": "PENDING",
  "appointmentDate": "2026-03-10T00:00:00.000Z",   // ISO-8601 UTC string w/ ms; from new Date(body.appointmentDate)
  "startTime": "09:00",             // plain string, NOT a date
  "endTime": "09:30",               // plain string
  "reason": "string" | null,
  "notes": null,
  "appointmentType": "IN_PERSON",   // enum IN_PERSON|VIDEO|PHONE|WALK_IN, echoed from body
  "confirmedAt": null,
  "completedAt": null,
  "cancelledAt": null,
  "cancelReason": null,
  "recurringRule": null,
  "recurringGroupId": null,
  "createdAt": "2026-09-03T10:22:41.512Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-09-03T10:22:41.512Z",
  "deletedAt": null,
  "clinic": { "name": "Nile Clinic" },              // ONLY name — no id/address/phone (GET / returns those)
  "physician": { "user": { "displayName": "Dr. Ahmed" } },  // no physician id, no specialty
  "subprofile": null | { "name": "Noor", "relation": "CHILD" }  // enum SELF|SPOUSE|CHILD|PARENT|SIBLING|OTHER; null (present, not omitted) when no subprofile
}
errorCases: 401 {"error":"No token provided"} when Authorization header missing or not starting with 'Bearer '
401 {"error":"Invalid token"} when jwt.verify throws (bad signature, expired)
400 {"error":"All booking fields are required"} when ANY of clinicId, physicianUserId, appointmentDate, startTime, endTime is falsy (empty string counts as missing)
400 {"error":"Physician not found"} when no PhysicianProfile exists for body.physicianUserId — note 400, NOT 404
409 {"error":"This slot is already booked"} when a PENDING/CONFIRMED appointment for that PhysicianProfile exists on the same local day with the identical startTime string

500 {"error":"Failed to book appointment"} on any thrown error: nonexistent clinicId (FK violation), nonexistent subprofileId (FK violation), unparseable appointmentDate (Invalid Date), appointmentType not in the AppointmentType enum
429 {"error":"Too many requests, please try again later"} from the global /api limiter (100 req/min per IP, standardHeaders on)
requestBody: clinicId: string — REQUIRED
physicianUserId: string (User.id of the doctor, not the profile id) — REQUIRED
appointmentDate: string 'YYYY-MM-DD' (what the client sends) — REQUIRED
startTime: string 'HH:MM' — REQUIRED
endTime: string 'HH:MM' — REQUIRED
reason: string — optional; '' is coerced to null
appointmentType: string — optional; defaults to 'IN_PERSON'; NOT validated
subprofileId: string — optional; '' or undefined coerced to null; NOT verified to belong to the caller
dbWrites: appointments — 1 INSERT, NOT in a transaction
notifications — 1 INSERT via notificationService.createNotification, best-effort inside its own try/catch, NOT in a transaction
crossModelReads: PhysicianProfile (findUnique by userId)
Clinic (read via prisma include, select name)
FamilySubprofile (read via prisma include, select name+relation)
User (findUnique of the caller for displayName, used only in the notification text)
User (again, inside notificationService, select email+displayName for the email dispatch)
Notification (write)
DeviceToken (read inside pushService.send)
sideEffects: Notification row for the physician: type 'NEW_APPOINTMENT_REQUEST', title 'New Appointment Request', message `${patientDisplayName||'A patient'}${subprofile? ' (for '+name+')':''} booked an appointment on ${toLocaleDateString('en-US',{weekday:'short',month:'short',day:'numeric'})} at ${startTime}${reason? ' — '+reason:''}.`

Transactional EMAIL to the physician (sendEmail: true) — awaited synchronously inside the request; subject = title, html = `

${title}

${message}

`
FCM push attempt to the physician (pushService.send is always tried by createNotification, errors swallowed)
NO cache invalidation — GET / and GET /today are cacheMiddleware(15) and keep serving the pre-booking list for up to 15s for that same user
externalDeps: lib/cacheMiddleware — NOT used on this route, but its stale window is a consequence of this write
quirks: Books for the CALLER, not for a named patient: data.patientUserId = req.user.id. The body has no patient field at all, so a physician or receptionist hitting POST / creates an appointment with THEMSELVES as the patient.
Missing physician profile returns 400, not 404, with the message 'Physician not found'.

clinicId is NEVER validated — not checked to exist, not checked to belong to the physician, and clinic.allowPatientBooking is NOT enforced here (only GET /available honors it). A patient can book at a booking-disabled clinic by POSTing directly.
No TimeSlot validation whatsoever: any startTime/endTime string is accepted, including out-of-hours values and non-time garbage ('banana' is stored verbatim).
The conflict query omits clinicId, so it spans ALL of that physician's clinics — the physician cannot be double-booked across two clinics at the same minute.
The conflict query ignores endTime and any overlap logic: only an EXACTLY equal startTime string collides. 09:00-10:00 and 09:30-10:30 both succeed.

The day window is built as new Date(appointmentDate) then LOCAL setHours(0,0,0,0)/setHours(23,59,59,999). V8 parses 'YYYY-MM-DD' as UTC midnight, so on a UTC-negative host the window covers the PREVIOUS local day and the collision check silently looks at the wrong day.

appointmentDate is stored as the UTC-midnight instant of the 'YYYY-MM-DD' string, and it serializes back as '...T00:00:00.000Z'. Compare POST /walk-in, which parses the same input as LOCAL 12:00 — the two endpoints store different instants for the same date string.
findFirst-then-create is not atomic and there is no unique index, so two concurrent bookings for the same slot both return 201.
CANCELLED / COMPLETED / NO_SHOW appointments do not block a rebooking (status filter is only ['PENDING','CONFIRMED']).
appointmentType comes straight from the body with no whitelist; a value outside the enum makes Prisma throw and the client sees 500 'Failed to book appointment', not a 400.
reason: '' becomes null (|| null), so an empty reason is indistinguishable from no reason.
subprofileId is not checked against the caller's own PatientProfile — any known subprofile UUID is accepted (only the FK guards existence).

Notification type is the string 'NEW_APPOINTMENT_REQUEST', which is NOT in notificationService.NOTIFICATION_TYPES (that list contains 'APPOINTMENT_BOOKED'). Notification.type is a plain String column so it persists unvalidated; any client-side switch on the documented type list will not match it.
The entire notification+email block is wrapped in its own try/catch that only logs — a dead SMTP server or missing physician still returns 201 and the response says nothing about it.
The notification date string is produced by toLocaleDateString('en-US', …) in the SERVER's timezone from a UTC-midnight Date, so it can name the previous day on UTC-negative hosts.
The notification is addressed to body.physicianUserId (a User.id) while the appointment stores physician.id (a profile id) — two different identifiers in one flow.
The response's clinic object has ONLY { name }. GET /api/appointments returns clinic { id, name, address, phone } for the same rows, so the client sees a narrower clinic here.
The response has NO patientUser key, while GET / and GET /today add patientUser: { id, displayName, phone } | null. A client reusing one renderer must tolerate its absence.
subprofile is emitted as null (key present) rather than omitted when there is no family member.

Every string in req.body was already mutated by the global XSS sanitizer in server/src/index.js L56-L81 before this handler ran: <script>…</script> and a tag blacklist are stripped, /\bon\w+\s*=…/ handlers are stripped, the substrings 'javascript:', 'data:' and 'vbscript:' are removed ANYWHERE in the string (so a reason of 'data: 5mg' is stored as ' 5mg'), 'expression(' is removed, and 'url(' is rewritten to 'url\('. A faithful port must replicate this or stored reason text differs.
deletedAt is always present and always null: this router never writes it and never filters on it, so the soft-delete column is decorative.

endpoints.summary: Creates a series of up to 12 appointments spaced by a fixed day interval derived from `rule`, all sharing a generated recurringGroupId, with patientUserId = the CALLER. Sequential un-transacted inserts, no conflict checking, no notification. Returns { count, groupId, appointments: [...] }.
endpoints.auth: router.use(authCheck) at L19 — JWT Bearer only. No aiUsageCheck, no auditLog. NO in-handler gate at all: no userType check, no clinic ownership check, no staff check, no allowPatientBooking check. Any authenticated user can create a 12-deep series against any physicianUserId and any clinicId.
endpoints.responseShape:
{
  "count": 4,                       // created.length — the ACTUAL rows inserted, not the requested count
  "groupId": "uuid",                // response key differs from the model field, which is recurringGroupId
  "appointments": [                 // ordered oldest-first; CAN BE AN EMPTY ARRAY (never null) — see quirks
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "clinicId": "uuid",
      "physicianId": "uuid",
      "patientUserId": "uuid",      // always req.user.id
      "subprofileId": null,          // not settable on this route
      "clinicPatientId": null,
      "status": "PENDING",
      "appointmentDate": "2026-03-10T00:00:00.000Z",
      "startTime": "09:00",
      "endTime": "09:30",
      "reason": "string" | null,
      "notes": null,
      "appointmentType": "IN_PERSON",   // not settable on this route; schema default
      "confirmedAt": null,
      "completedAt": null,
      "cancelledAt": null,
      "cancelReason": null,
      "recurringRule": "WEEKLY",        // stored VERBATIM from the body, unvalidated
      "recurringGroupId": "uuid",       // same value as the top-level groupId
      "createdAt": "2026-09-03T10:22:41.512Z",
      "updatedAt": "2026-09-03T10:22:41.512Z",
      "deletedAt": null
    }
  ]
}
// NOTE: no include — the array elements have NO clinic, NO physician, NO subprofile, NO patientUser keys, unlike POST /.
errorCases: 401 {"error":"No token provided"} / 401 {"error":"Invalid token"} from authCheck
400 {"error":"All fields required"} when ANY of clinicId, physicianUserId, startDate, startTime, endTime, rule is falsy (`count` is NOT required)
400 {"error":"Physician not found"} when no PhysicianProfile exists for body.physicianUserId — 400, not 404

500 {"error":"Failed to create recurring appointments"} on a thrown error mid-loop (bad clinicId FK, unparseable startDate) — earlier occurrences in the series are ALREADY COMMITTED and are not rolled back
429 {"error":"Too many requests, please try again later"} from the global /api limiter
requestBody: clinicId: string — REQUIRED
physicianUserId: string (User.id) — REQUIRED
startDate: string 'YYYY-MM-DD' — REQUIRED
startTime: string 'HH:MM' — REQUIRED
endTime: string 'HH:MM' — REQUIRED
rule: string — REQUIRED; only 'WEEKLY' and 'BIWEEKLY' are recognized, everything else falls through to a 30-day interval
reason: string — optional; '' coerced to null
count: number — optional; Math.min(count || 4, 12)
dbWrites: appointments — N sequential individual INSERTs in a for-loop, explicitly NOT wrapped in prisma.$transaction; a failure at iteration k leaves iterations 0..k-1 committed
crossModelReads: PhysicianProfile (findUnique by userId)
sideEffects: NONE — no notification, no email, no push, no audit row, no cache invalidation. This is the only create route here that notifies nobody.
GET / and GET /today (cacheMiddleware(15)) can stay stale for up to 15s after the series is created
externalDeps: node:crypto (require('crypto').randomUUID() called lazily inside the handler for groupId)
quirks: Books for the CALLER: patientUserId = req.user.id. body.physicianUserId is the doctor; there is no way to create a series on behalf of a patient.

count is clamped on the HIGH side only: Math.min(count || 4, 12). count: 0 → falsy → 4. count: -3 → Math.min(-3,12) = -3 → the loop body never runs → **201 with {count: 0, groupId: '<uuid>', appointments: []}** and a groupId that belongs to nothing. A non-numeric count → NaN → 0 < NaN is false → same empty 201. count: 100 → 12.
`appointments` can therefore be an EMPTY ARRAY on a 201 — never null, but a client that assumes at least one row will break.

intervalDays = rule === 'WEEKLY' ? 7 : rule === 'BIWEEKLY' ? 14 : 30. 'MONTHLY', 'DAILY', 'YEARLY', lowercase 'weekly', and outright typos ALL silently become 30-day spacing, while recurringRule stores the unrecognized string verbatim — the persisted rule and the actual spacing disagree.
'MONTHLY' is 30 calendar days, not a calendar month, so a Jan 31 start lands on Mar 2, Apr 1, May 1 — the day-of-month drifts.
ZERO conflict checking. Unlike POST /, there is no 409 path: the series can stack on top of existing PENDING/CONFIRMED appointments, on other patients' bookings, and on itself.
NOT transactional. Sequential prisma.appointment.create calls in a plain for-loop, so a mid-series failure returns 500 while leaving orphaned committed occurrences the client never learns the ids of.
No notification of any kind is sent — the physician is never told a 12-appointment series was booked against their calendar. Inconsistent with POST /, /confirm and /cancel.
subprofileId is not read from the body → always null. A recurring series cannot be booked for a family member.
appointmentType is not read from the body → always the IN_PERSON schema default; notes always null.
The response key is `groupId` while the column is `recurringGroupId` — the same value appears under two different names in one payload.

`count` in the response is created.length, the actual insert count, not the requested/clamped count. They diverge only in the negative/NaN case described above (where both happen to be 0) but a port must return the array length, not the clamp result.

Date math is JS-Date-specific: `const date = new Date(startDate)` is RE-parsed from the original string on every iteration (so no compounding drift), then `date.setDate(date.getDate() + (i * intervalDays))` mutates using LOCAL date components on a UTC-midnight instant. On a UTC-negative host getDate() returns the previous day, and a DST boundary inside the series shifts the stored UTC instant by ±1 hour relative to occurrence 0. Occurrence k is therefore NOT simply start + k*interval in UTC — a .NET port using UTC DateTime arithmetic will produce different appointmentDate values.
The 400 message is the bare 'All fields required' — shorter and different from POST /'s 'All booking fields are required'. Two near-identical validations with two different strings.
clinicId is never validated against the physician or for existence — an invalid one surfaces as 500, not 400/403.
Same global XSS sanitizer applies to `reason` before the handler runs (see server/src/index.js L56-L81).

endpoints.summary: Creates an immediately-CONFIRMED WALK_IN appointment for a named patient, resolving the physician either from the caller's own PhysicianProfile or (staff path) from the clinic's physicianId. Then runs two independent best-effort blocks: notify the physician, and auto-insert the patient into today's waitingQueue with the next queue number. Returns only the appointment plus clinic.name.
endpoints.auth: router.use(authCheck) at L19 — JWT Bearer only. No aiUsageCheck, no auditLog. In-handler gate: if the caller has ANY PhysicianProfile they are accepted unconditionally (physicianId = their own profile, no clinic ownership check); otherwise an ACTIVE ClinicStaff row for that exact clinicId is required, else 403. ClinicStaff.role and ClinicStaff.permissions are never consulted.
endpoints.responseShape:
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "clinicId": "uuid",
  "physicianId": "uuid",
  "patientUserId": "uuid",          // straight from the body, NOT FK-validated
  "subprofileId": "uuid" | null,
  "clinicPatientId": null,
  "status": "CONFIRMED",            // hard-coded, walk-ins skip PENDING
  "appointmentDate": "2026-09-03T09:00:00.000Z",  // = new Date(body.appointmentDate + 'T12:00:00') i.e. server-LOCAL noon; or `now` (full timestamp incl. time-of-day) when appointmentDate is absent
  "startTime": "14:35",             // body.startTime, else server-local HH:MM of now
  "endTime": "14:35",               // body.endTime, else EQUAL to startTime (zero-length appointment)
  "reason": "Walk-in",              // body.reason, else the literal string 'Walk-in' — never null
  "notes": "WALK_IN",               // hard-coded literal
  "appointmentType": "WALK_IN",     // hard-coded
  "confirmedAt": "2026-09-03T11:35:02.881Z",  // = now
  "completedAt": null,
  "cancelledAt": null,
  "cancelReason": null,
  "recurringRule": null,
  "recurringGroupId": null,
  "createdAt": "2026-09-03T11:35:02.881Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-09-03T11:35:02.881Z",
  "deletedAt": null,
  "clinic": { "name": "Nile Clinic" }   // ONLY include on this route
}
// physician, subprofile, patientUser, the created waitingQueue row, and the queueNumber are ALL ABSENT (keys not present, not null).
errorCases: 401 {"error":"No token provided"} / 401 {"error":"Invalid token"} from authCheck
400 {"error":"clinicId and patientUserId are required"} when either is falsy
403 {"error":"Not authorized"} when the caller has no PhysicianProfile AND no active ClinicStaff row for that clinicId
404 {"error":"Clinic not found"} — reachable ONLY on the staff path (a physician caller never gets this; a bad clinicId becomes a 500 for them)

500 {"error":"Failed to create walk-in"} on a thrown error: nonexistent clinicId (FK violation on the physician path), nonexistent subprofileId (FK violation), or an Invalid Date from appointmentDate + 'T12:00:00' when the client sends anything other than 'YYYY-MM-DD'
429 {"error":"Too many requests, please try again later"} from the global /api limiter
requestBody: clinicId: string — REQUIRED
patientUserId: string — REQUIRED; NOT FK-constrained and NOT validated
reason: string — optional; defaults to the literal 'Walk-in'
appointmentDate: string 'YYYY-MM-DD' — optional; defaults to `now`
startTime: string 'HH:MM' — optional; defaults to server-local HH:MM of now
endTime: string 'HH:MM' — optional; defaults to resolvedStart (equal to startTime)
subprofileId: string — optional; '' (the client's empty form field) coerced to null
dbWrites: appointments — 1 INSERT, NOT in a transaction
notifications — 1 conditional INSERT via notificationService, best-effort try/catch
waiting_queues — 1 conditional INSERT (auto-check-in), best-effort try/catch, NOT transactional and NOT atomic with the queueNumber read
crossModelReads: PhysicianProfile (findUnique by userId; then findUnique by id twice more — once for the notification, once for the queue row)
ClinicStaff (findFirst, staff path only)
Clinic (findUnique select physicianId, staff path only; plus Clinic read via the include for name)
User (findUnique select displayName — twice: once for the notification, once for the queue patientName)
FamilySubprofile (findUnique select name, only when subprofileId is present)
WaitingQueue (findFirst for an existing WAITING/BEING_SEEN row; findFirst orderBy queueNumber desc for the next number; then create)
Notification (write)
DeviceToken (read inside pushService.send)
sideEffects: Notification to the physician ONLY when physicianProfile.userId !== req.user.id: type 'PATIENT_ARRIVED', title 'Walk-in Patient', message `${displayName||'A patient'} has been added as a walk-in at ${appointment.clinic?.name || 'your clinic'}`. sendEmail is NOT passed → no email. Failures are logger.warn only.

Auto-check-in: a waiting_queues row with source 'APPOINTMENT' (not 'WALK_IN'), status defaulting to 'WAITING', queueNumber = (max for that clinic TODAY) + 1, queueDate = TODAY's local midnight, appointmentId = the new appointment id, reason = reason || 'Walk-in', patientName = subprofile name || user.displayName || 'Patient', subprofileName = the subprofile name or null, physicianUserId = physicianProfile?.userId || req.user.id. Skipped entirely if the patient already has a WAITING/BEING_SEEN row for that clinic today. Failures are logger.warn only.
logger.info('[WalkIn] Auto-checked-in patient <id> as #<n>') on a successful queue insert
FCM push attempt via pushService (only when the notification block runs)
NO cache invalidation — GET / and GET /today stay stale for up to 15s
externalDeps: services/emailService is NOT reached here (sendEmail omitted → false)
quirks: The physician branch takes precedence and performs NO ownership check: if the caller has any PhysicianProfile, physicianId = THEIR OWN profile id regardless of which clinicId was passed. A physician can create a walk-in in another physician's clinic and it is attributed to themselves. clinicId existence is enforced only by the FK, so on this branch a bad clinic yields 500, never 404.
404 'Clinic not found' is unreachable for a physician caller — the same bad input produces 403/404/500 depending on WHO calls.

patientUserId has NO Prisma relation on Appointment (plain String column, no FK) and is never validated. Any arbitrary string is accepted and stored; the appointment then renders with a null patient everywhere downstream.

Date parsing differs from POST /: `new Date(appointmentDate + 'T12:00:00')` is server-LOCAL noon, whereas POST / uses `new Date(appointmentDate)` = UTC midnight. The two endpoints persist DIFFERENT instants for the identical 'YYYY-MM-DD' input. A port must keep both behaviours distinct.
If the client ever sends a full ISO timestamp instead of 'YYYY-MM-DD', the string concatenation produces an unparseable value → Invalid Date → Prisma throws → 500, not a 400.

When appointmentDate is omitted, appointmentDate is set to `now` — a full timestamp with a real time-of-day, not a normalized midnight/noon. Walk-in rows are therefore inconsistent with every other appointment row's date normalization.
endTime defaults to resolvedStart, producing a ZERO-LENGTH appointment where endTime === startTime.

Mixed-source date/time: supplying appointmentDate but not startTime takes the DATE from the body and the TIME from server-local `now`, with no consistency check — a walk-in dated next Tuesday gets today's clock time.
reason is never null on this route — it defaults to the literal string 'Walk-in'. Client code that tests `reason == null` will never see it.
notes is hard-set to the literal 'WALK_IN'. GET /queue detects check-in by `notes?.includes('CHECKIN:')`, so a walk-in reads as NOT checked in even though it was auto-queued.
status 'CONFIRMED' and confirmedAt = now are set on creation — walk-ins never pass through PENDING, so no /confirm step exists for them.
NO duplicate or slot-conflict check at all (unlike POST /'s 409). The same patient can be walked in repeatedly at the same minute; each call creates another appointment.
The notification is suppressed when the physician adds their own walk-in (physicianProfile.userId === req.user.id) — a silent no-op that is not reflected in the response.
The auto-check-in uses TODAY's local midnight for queueDate, NOT resolvedDate. A walk-in dated in the future is still queued for today, so appointmentDate and queueDate disagree.
waiting_queues.source is set to 'APPOINTMENT', not 'WALK_IN', contradicting both the route name and the column's own schema default of 'WALK_IN'.

queueNumber is computed by a separate findFirst(orderBy queueNumber desc) and then incremented outside any transaction → duplicate queue numbers under concurrency. It also scans ALL statuses for that clinic+day (including COMPLETED and CANCELLED), so numbers are never reused and monotonically grow.

If the patient already has a WAITING or BEING_SEEN row for that clinic today, the appointment is still created but NO new queue row is added — the 201 body is identical either way and gives the client no way to tell.

subprofileName on the queue row is populated only when the FamilySubprofile lookup actually returns a row; if subprofileId was stored on the appointment but the row is missing, subprofileName stays null while patientName silently falls back to the account holder's displayName.
waiting_queues.physicianUserId falls back to req.user.id when the PhysicianProfile lookup returns nothing — a staff member's own id can end up in the physician column.

BOTH post-create blocks (notification and auto-check-in) are wrapped in try/catch → logger.warn. A completely failed check-in still returns 201 with a body that looks like a success, and the client (AssistantDashboardPage) has to re-fetch /queue to discover the truth.

The 201 body carries ONLY the appointment + clinic.name. It does NOT include the queue row, the assigned queueNumber, the physician, the subprofile, or the patient — physician/subprofile/patientUser keys are ABSENT (not null), unlike POST /'s response.
This route ignores the X-Clinic-Id header entirely (only GET / reads it) — clinicId must be in the body.
Same global XSS sanitizer applies to reason before the handler runs (server/src/index.js L56-L81).
The client (client/src/pages/AppointmentsPage.jsx L436) POSTs the whole walkInForm object including subprofileId: '' — the '' → null coercion is load-bearing.

endpoints.summary: Staff or physician writes a pre-visit intake note. Looks the appointment up only to derive the physician's userId and the patient's userId, then CREATES (never really updates — see quirks) a PatientNote whose content is prefixed '[INTAKE by <callerUserId>]', and notifies the physician when the writer is not the physician. Returns the PatientNote row spread with a message key, at status 200.
endpoints.auth: router.use(authCheck) at L19 — JWT Bearer only. No aiUsageCheck, no auditLog. In-handler gate: physician-owner of the appointment (PhysicianProfile.id === appt.physicianId) OR any ACTIVE ClinicStaff row at appt.clinicId, else 403. The docblock claims 'clinic staff with canDraftNotes' but permissions.canDraftNotes is NEVER read. There is NO validateConnection check (unlike PUT /api/patient-notes/:patientUserId).
endpoints.responseShape:
{
  "id": "uuid",                    // PatientNote.id
  "physicianUserId": "uuid",        // isPhysician ? req.user.id : appt.physician.user.id
  "patientUserId": "uuid",          // appt.patientUserId
  "subprofileId": null,             // ALWAYS null — never copied from appt.subprofileId
  "clinicPatientId": null,          // never set
  "content": "[INTAKE by 3f2a1c88-…-9d41]\nPatient reports chest pain for 3 days",  // literal author UUID, then \n, then note.trim()
  "isPinned": false,
  "createdAt": "2026-09-03T11:41:07.204Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-09-03T11:41:07.204Z",
  "message": "Intake note saved"    // appended by the handler, NOT a model field
}
// No appointmentId, no patient name, no physician object — the note is not linked to the appointment at all.
errorCases: 401 {"error":"No token provided"} / 401 {"error":"Invalid token"} from authCheck
400 {"error":"Note content required"} when note is undefined/null/'' or whitespace-only (guard is `!note?.trim()`)
404 {"error":"Appointment not found"} when no Appointment matches :id

403 {"error":"Not authorized to write intake notes"} when the caller is neither the owning physician nor active staff at appt.clinicId — note the LONGER message, unlike the bare 'Not authorized' used elsewhere in this file

500 {"error":"Failed to save intake note"} on any throw — most importantly the Prisma P2002 unique-constraint violation on PatientNote @@unique([physicianUserId, patientUserId, subprofileId]) that fires on the SECOND intake note for the same physician+patient (or the FIRST, if /api/patient-notes already created that row)

500 {"error":"Failed to save intake note"} when `note` is a non-string (number, object, array): `note?.trim` is undefined, calling it throws TypeError, and the outer catch converts it to a 500 instead of the intended 400
429 {"error":"Too many requests, please try again later"} from the global /api limiter
requestBody: note: string — REQUIRED, must be non-empty after .trim(); no maximum length is enforced here
dbWrites: patient_notes — 1 INSERT (the UPDATE branch is dead code, see quirks), NOT in a transaction
notifications — 1 conditional INSERT via notificationService, best-effort try/catch
crossModelReads: PhysicianProfile (findUnique by userId; plus the full PhysicianProfile row + nested User via the appointment's include)
User (nested select id via the appointment include; plus findUnique select displayName for the notification text)
ClinicStaff (findFirst, only when the caller is not the owning physician)
PatientNote (findFirst with content startsWith filter; then create or update)
Notification (write)
DeviceToken (read inside pushService.send)
sideEffects: Notification to the physician, ONLY when the writer is not the physician: type 'INTAKE_NOTE_READY', title 'Intake Note Ready', message `Pre-visit intake note written for ${displayName||'patient'} (${appt.startTime})`, data { appointmentId, noteId, patientUserId }. sendEmail not passed → no email. Failures are logger.warn only.
Mutates a PatientNote row that /api/patient-notes also owns — the two routes fight over the same unique key
quirks: Returns 200 even when it CREATES the note — never 201. A port that follows REST convention here breaks the contract.

The 400 guard `!note?.trim()` only protects against nullish and empty strings. A NON-STRING note (e.g. 123, {}, []) makes `note?.trim` undefined, the call throws TypeError, and the client receives 500 'Failed to save intake note' instead of the 400 the guard was meant to produce.

THE DEDUPE LOOKUP IS BROKEN AND THE UPDATE BRANCH IS DEAD CODE. The handler searches `content: { startsWith: '[INTAKE]' }` (L1161) but writes `` `[INTAKE by ${userId}]\n…` `` (L1156). '[INTAKE by …]' does not start with the literal '[INTAKE]', and grepping the whole repo shows nothing ever writes '[INTAKE]'. Every call therefore takes the create path.

CONSEQUENCE: PatientNote carries @@unique([physicianUserId, patientUserId, subprofileId]) and this route always writes subprofileId = null, so the SECOND intake note for the same physician+patient raises P2002 and the client gets 500 'Failed to save intake note'. It also collides with a note already created by PUT /api/patient-notes/:patientUserId (which upserts on the very same key with subprofileId: null), so even the FIRST intake note can 500. This is the highest-value quirk on this endpoint — a port that 'fixes' it into a real upsert changes observable behaviour.

Conversely, /api/patient-notes' upsert (server/src/routes/patientNotes.js L99) writes to the SAME row and silently overwrites the '[INTAKE by …]' content — the intake draft can vanish without a trace.
No length cap here, while /api/patient-notes rejects content > 5000 chars with 400. An intake note can exceed 5000 chars and then be un-editable through the other route.

subprofileId is never copied from appt.subprofileId → always null. An intake note for a child's appointment is filed under the ACCOUNT HOLDER, not the family member, and is therefore indistinguishable from the account holder's own note.
clinicPatientId is never set even though the model supports it and the appointment could be tied to a ClinicPatient.
The content embeds the raw author UUID, not a display name: '[INTAKE by 3f2a1c88-…]'. The client renders this string verbatim.
The docblock's 'clinic staff with canDraftNotes' permission is never checked — ANY active ClinicStaff row at appt.clinicId can write clinical notes.

No connection validation: unlike /api/patient-notes (which calls validateConnection and 403s with 'Not connected to this patient'), this route lets clinic staff write notes about a patient the physician has no connection to.
The 403 message is 'Not authorized to write intake notes' — different from the bare 'Not authorized' used by /confirm, /cancel, /complete, /no-show and DELETE /:id in the same file.

physicianUserId is derived as `isPhysician ? req.user.id : appt.physician.user.id`. Both branches resolve to the same value in practice (isPhysician requires appt.physicianId === physician.id), so the ternary is redundant but must be preserved because a future data inconsistency would diverge.

The notification is skipped entirely when the physician writes their own note (`if (!isPhysician)`), and the whole block is try/catch → logger.warn, so the 200 says nothing about whether anyone was told.

The :id path param is used ONLY to look up the appointment and derive patient/physician. The note is NOT linked to the appointment in any column — two different appointments for the same patient share the single PatientNote row, and the response contains no appointmentId.

Route order: POST /walk-in (L556) and POST /recurring (L700) are registered before this two-segment route, so there is no shadowing; but any :id value is accepted (Appointment.id is a text column, not @db.Uuid, so a non-UUID id simply misses and returns 404 rather than a cast error).

The note string was already mutated by the global XSS sanitizer (server/src/index.js L56-L81) before .trim() ran: tag blacklist stripped, on*= handlers stripped, 'javascript:'/'data:'/'vbscript:' removed anywhere in the text (clinically relevant for a note mentioning 'data:'), 'expression(' removed, and 'url(' rewritten to 'url\('.

endpoints.summary: Permanently HARD-deletes an appointment row. Allows the owning physician, the patient themselves, or any active clinic staff at the appointment's clinic. No status restriction, no notification, no dependent cleanup. Returns a bare message object.
endpoints.auth: router.use(authCheck) at L19 — JWT Bearer only. No aiUsageCheck, no auditLog. In-handler gate: isPhysician (PhysicianProfile.id === appt.physicianId) OR isPatient (appt.patientUserId === req.user.id) OR an ACTIVE ClinicStaff row at appt.clinicId (queried ONLY when the first two are false), else 403.
endpoints.responseShape:
{ "message": "Appointment deleted" }
// That is the entire body. No id, no deletedCount, no echo of the removed row, no `success` flag.
errorCases: 401 {"error":"No token provided"} / 401 {"error":"Invalid token"} from authCheck

404 {"error":"Appointment not found"} when no Appointment matches :id — this is ALSO what `DELETE /api/appointments/slots` (no slot id) returns, because it falls through to this handler with id === 'slots'
403 {"error":"Not authorized"} when the caller is not the owning physician, not the patient, and not active staff at appt.clinicId

500 {"error":"Failed to delete appointment"} on a thrown error — notably Prisma P2025 when a concurrent request already deleted the row between the findUnique and the delete (the client sees 500, not 404)
429 {"error":"Too many requests, please try again later"} from the global /api limiter
dbWrites: appointments — 1 hard DELETE (prisma.appointment.delete), NOT in a transaction and NOT atomic with the preceding findUnique
crossModelReads: PhysicianProfile (findUnique by userId)
ClinicStaff (findFirst — only evaluated when the caller is neither the owning physician nor the patient)
sideEffects: NONE beyond the row removal: no notification, no email, no push, no audit row, no cache invalidation.
Orphans are left behind: payments.appointmentId, waiting_queues.appointmentId and video_sessions.appointmentId keep pointing at the vanished id
quirks: This is a HARD delete (prisma.appointment.delete), even though Appointment carries a `deletedAt DateTime?` soft-delete column documented as 'null means active'. Nothing in this router ever writes or filters deletedAt — a port must hard-delete, not soft-delete.

Route-order shadowing: router.delete('/slots/:id') is registered at L96, long before this handler at L928, so DELETE /api/appointments/slots/<uuid> deactivates a TimeSlot (isActive: false) and never reaches here. But DELETE /api/appointments/slots — one path segment, no id — DOES match this route with id === 'slots' and returns 404 {"error":"Appointment not found"}.
THE PATIENT IS ALLOWED TO DELETE. isPatient (appt.patientUserId === req.user.id) is in the allow-list, so a patient can permanently erase clinic records from the physician's calendar.
No status restriction at all: a COMPLETED, CANCELLED or NO_SHOW appointment is just as deletable as a PENDING one. Completed-visit history disappears with it.

Authorization short-circuits: the ClinicStaff query is skipped entirely when isPhysician or isPatient is true, so the staff branch is only reachable for third parties. A port that always runs the staff query would issue an extra read but must not change the outcome.
The physician check is identity-based (appt.physicianId === physician.id), so a DIFFERENT physician practising at the same clinic gets 403 unless they also hold an active ClinicStaff row there.

NO notification is sent to anyone. The patient is never told their appointment was erased, and the physician is never told a patient erased it — asymmetric with /confirm and /cancel, which both notify (and /cancel even emails).

Nothing cleans up dependents. payments.appointmentId, waiting_queues.appointmentId and video_sessions.appointmentId are plain `String?` columns with NO Prisma relation and NO database FK, so the delete always succeeds and leaves dangling references. A .NET/SQL Server port that introduces real foreign keys here will start failing this endpoint (or cascade-deleting payments) unless those columns stay unconstrained.

The findUnique-then-delete pair is not atomic. Two concurrent deletes: the first returns 200, the second throws P2025 inside the delete and surfaces as 500 'Failed to delete appointment' rather than the 404 the pre-check was meant to give.

No cache invalidation. GET / and GET /today are wrapped in cacheMiddleware(15) keyed `route:<userId>:<originalUrl>` in an in-process memory cache, so the deleted appointment can keep appearing in that same user's list for up to 15 seconds — and because the cache is per-process, under PM2 cluster mode the staleness is nondeterministic across workers.
Appointment.id is a plain text column (String @id @default(uuid()) with no @db.Uuid), so a malformed/non-UUID :id causes no cast error — it simply misses and returns 404.
The success body has no `deletedAt`, no `id`, and no status echo — a client cannot confirm WHICH row went away from the response alone.
